newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: South African stocks ended cautiously higher on Wednesday as a recovering bullion price spurred the flagging gold index into a much-needed advance, dealers said.

The afternoon London gold price fixed at $380.85 an ounce, above the crucial psychological barrier of $380. The firmer price pushed up gold shares, but negative sentiment elsewhere in the market held industrials and the over-all index back.
"Golds rose on the bullion price, but people have generally been quite wary in this market this week," said one dealer.
Negative reserves data on Friday gave the market a hangover that has prevented it from joining the bullish party enjoyed by London's FTSE-100 and Wall Street this week.
The all-share index finished up 10.5 points to 7,046.8 in good volumes as golds rose 18.6 points to 1,746.5. The industrials index edged up 12.7 points to 8,258.4.
But dealers said they had taken some heart from economic data released on Tuesday that was in line with expectations.
The producer price index (PPI) rose 1.0 percent in August from July after rising 0.8 percent in July. A Reuters consensus poll of economists forecast PPI would rise 0.9 percent month-on-month.
The South African Chamber of Commerce Business Confidence Index (BCI) dipped to its lowest level in a year as the September index dropped 1.1 percent to 115.9.

Dealers said the figures, while not particularly positive in themselves, had been as expected and so boosted the market. "The market was turning slightly negative when they came out and it turned positive afterwards," one dealer said.
"People were happy to get things as expected," he added.
Dealers said if Wall Street continued its strong gains and held levels above 6,000 then South Africa's market could make some upward strides on Wednesday.
"It all depends on Wall Street. If the Dow breaks through 6,000 then we could see this market really running," one dealer said.

Following Monday's trend there was some strong buying in blue chips as South African Breweries rose 75 cents to 122 rand and Iscor nudged up three cents to end at 304 cents in heavy trade that saw 3.23 million shares change hands.
"SAB has been on everybody's lips and now it is on everybody's sheets," one dealer said.
Dealers said there had been some strong buying by South African institutions and some selling by foreigners.
Light trade in futures saw the all-share December contract rise up to 6,637/55 from 6,615 as golds rose to 1,236/38 from 1,231. The industrials contract slipped to 8,155/60 from 8,167.
